text: A generator is a function that produces values one at a time, using yield instead of return.
Each time the generator is asked for a value, it runs until it hits yield, then pauses right there.
So countdown yields three, then two, then one, resuming exactly where it left off each time.
[chuckle] This fibonacci generator yields numbers on the fly, never building the whole sequence in memory.
Wrap it in list and you can collect them all, but the generator itself only holds one value at a time.
[sigh] That laziness is the whole point — this generator expression describes a million squares.
But nothing is computed until you ask — next pulls exactly one value, then the next call pulls another.
So you could iterate over billions of items using almost no memory at all.
[groan] Generators are Python's secret to handling huge or even infinite streams of data gracefully.
